argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than an unqualified certification defense. The admissible record supports certification on aggregate readiness grounds only as caveated compliance: the packet should defend certification on the basis of overall readiness while expressly preserving that the cybersecurity alert triage gap remains an unresolved material limitation issue for a named launch use case and therefore requires pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance under policy. That reframing answers the audit concern without claiming the materiality dispute is resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not offered as a basis to relax policy. The narrower request is that the auditor avoid unnecessary escalation beyond a caveated finding because the admissible evidence does support overall readiness, and the remaining dispute is specific and bounded to the unresolved handling of the named-use-case limitation.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not allow aggregate readiness, low traffic share, or clean rehearsal results to override a live disclosure predicate tied to a named launch use case. The admissible evidence shows the affected segment is named in two SOC deployment commitments and legal review is still open, so materiality is not resolved on the current record. The compliant reading is therefore conditional: certification is supportable only if the audit packet is treated as caveated compliance tied to the policy-required path of explicit disclosure of the limitation and monitoring posture before launch, or approved risk acceptance if disclosure will not be completed.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence in the current record that the required disclosure has already been completed before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case.
The product note describing the segment as non-core or low-volume does not resolve materiality given the named customer commitments.
Open legal review remains an unresolved indicator against treating the issue as fully cleared.
